motifs.name: material advantage for the side to move
motifs.description: The side to move has a net material edge of at least one pawn using standard piece values.
motifs.source:
import chess

MOTIF_NAME = 'material advantage for the side to move'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'The side to move has a net material edge of at least one pawn using standard piece values.'

_VALUES = {
    chess.PAWN: 100,
    chess.KNIGHT: 320,
    chess.BISHOP: 330,
    chess.ROOK: 500,
    chess.QUEEN: 900,
}


def motif(fen: str) -> bool:
    try:
        board = chess.Board(fen)
    except Exception:
        return False
    stm = board.turn
    opp = not stm
    diff = 0
    for pt, val in _VALUES.items():
        diff += val * (len(board.pieces(pt, stm)) - len(board.pieces(pt, opp)))
    return diff >= 100

motifs.name: positional dominance without material deficit
motifs.description: The side to move wins the overall balance of positional features (piece mobility, space, central control, passed pawns, pawn health, bishop pair, rook files, outposts) while not being behind in material.

motifs.name: permanent holes in the enemy camp
motifs.description: The side to move controls clearly more permanent weak squares deep in the opponent half - squares that no enemy pawn can ever attack again and that it already covers with at least as many units as the defender - than the opponent controls in its own half, while not being down material.

motifs.name: superior pawn structure and passed pawn edge
motifs.description: The side to move has a clearly healthier pawn skeleton than the opponent - more or further advanced passed pawns and fewer isolated, doubled, backward or scattered pawns - while not being down significant material.

motifs.name: enemy king stranded without shelter
motifs.description: With plenty of pieces still on the board and no material deficit for the side to move, the opponent's king is far worse sheltered than the king of the side to move: it sits on or near the central files, has lost the right to castle without reaching a corner, has drifted off its home rank, is missing the pawns that should stand in front of it, stands beside open or semi-open files, and/or is surrounded by enemy pieces. The side to move owns real attacking material (a queen or rook plus other pieces), so the exposed king is a concrete target.

motifs.name: safe piece infiltration in enemy territory
motifs.description: The side to move has clearly more securely posted active pieces inside the opponent half - units that no enemy pawn can hit now or after one push, that cannot be profitably captured, and that still have targets or free squares - than the opponent has in its own half, while not being down material.

motifs.name: space-gaining pawn wedge in the centre
motifs.description: The side to move owns a clear space advantage: several of its pawns (at least one on a central file) stand on the fourth rank or beyond and grip squares in the opponent half, none of these advanced pawns is over-attacked, and it is not behind in material.

motifs.name: opponent starved of forcing resources
motifs.description: The side to move owns concrete forcing resources - a capture that wins material, a safe check, a safe pawn push that hits an enemy piece, or a promotion - while the opponent, even if handed a free move, would have none or far fewer of them, so the whole initiative belongs to the side to move.

motifs.name: own camp free of enemy pressure
motifs.description: The side to move has nothing concrete to worry about at home: none of its pieces is hanging, harassed by a cheaper unit, over-attacked or pinned, no enemy piece or far advanced enemy pawn sits unchallenged inside its own half, and at most one enemy piece eyes the squares around its king.

motifs.name: opponent lags in mobilization and king shelter
motifs.description: With plenty of pieces still on the board and without being down material, the side to move is clearly better mobilized than the opponent: fewer minor pieces still on the first rank, less back-rank clutter, no corner-boxed rook, and a king already tucked away or free to castle while the opponent king sits in the centre or has wandered out.

motifs.name: pressure on weak squares around the enemy king
motifs.description: The side to move hits more completely undefended squares in the ring and front zone of the opponent king, with at least two attacking units and more total pressure there than the opponent generates around its own king.

motifs.name: pressure on the opponent weak pawns
motifs.description: The side to move puts more pressure on the opponent structurally weak or under-defended pawns (and harasses more enemy pieces with its own pawns) than the opponent does in return, while not being materially down.

motifs.name: opponent saddled with a bad minor piece
motifs.description: The opponent owns at least one clearly poor knight or bishop - almost no safe squares, still stuck on its home rank, rim-bound, or a bishop buried behind its own same-coloured and blocked pawns - while every minor piece of the side to move is healthy, with material roughly balanced.

motifs.name: winning capture with no counter-strike
motifs.description: The side to move has a capture whose full exchange sequence nets material and leaves it at least level in material, while the opponent, even if handed a free move, has no capture that wins as much back.
motifs.source:
import chess

_V = {chess.PAWN: 1, chess.KNIGHT: 3, chess.BISHOP: 3, chess.ROOK: 5, chess.QUEEN: 9, chess.KING: 100}

MOTIF_NAME = 'winning capture with no counter-strike'
MOTIF_DESCRIPTION = 'The side to move has a capture whose full exchange sequence nets material and leaves it at least level in material, while the opponent, even if handed a free move, has no capture that wins as much back.'


def _see(board, sq, side, att_val, vic_val):
    mine = sorted(_V[board.piece_type_at(s)] for s in board.attackers(side, sq))
    theirs = sorted(_V[board.piece_type_at(s)] for s in board.attackers(not side, sq))
    if att_val in mine:
        mine.remove(att_val)
    gains = [vic_val]
    occ = att_val
    ui = 0
    ti = 0
    other = True
    while True:
        if other:
            if ti >= len(theirs):
                break
            nxt = theirs[ti]
            ti += 1
        else:
            if ui >= len(mine):
                break
            nxt = mine[ui]
            ui += 1
        gains.append(occ - gains[-1])
        occ = nxt
        other = not other
    i = len(gains) - 1
    while i > 0:
        if gains[i - 1] > -gains[i]:
            gains[i - 1] = -gains[i]
        i -= 1
    return gains[0]


def _best_gain(board, side):
    targets = {}
    n = 0
    for mv in board.generate_legal_captures():
        n += 1
        if n > 90:
            break
        t = mv.to_square
        pt = board.piece_type_at(t)
        v = 1 if pt is None else _V[pt]
        a = _V[board.piece_type_at(mv.from_square)]
        prom = 0
        if mv.promotion:
            prom = 1
            v += 8
            a = 9
        key = (t, prom)
        cur = targets.get(key)
        if cur is None or a < cur[0]:
            targets[key] = (a, v)
    best = 0
    for key in targets:
        a, v = targets[key]
        g = _see(board, key[0], side, a, v)
        if g > best:
            best = g
    return best


def _mat(board, side):
    return (len(board.pieces(chess.PAWN, side))
            + 3 * len(board.pieces(chess.KNIGHT, side))
            + 3 * len(board.pieces(chess.BISHOP, side))
            + 5 * len(board.pieces(chess.ROOK, side))
            + 9 * len(board.pieces(chess.QUEEN, side)))


def motif(fen: str) -> bool:
    board = chess.Board(fen)
    if board.is_check():
        return False
    us = board.turn
    them = not us
    best_us = _best_gain(board, us)
    if best_us < 1:
        return False
    if _mat(board, us) - _mat(board, them) + best_us < 0:
        return False
    board.push(chess.Move.null())
    best_them = _best_gain(board, them)
    board.pop()
    if best_them < 0:
        best_them = 0
    return best_us - best_them >= 1

motifs.name: opponent pieces tied to passive defence
motifs.description: The opponent has clearly more pieces stuck in passive defensive duty than the side to move - non-pawn units that must guard an attacked friendly pawn, act as the only guard of an attacked unit, or sit in front of a passed pawn as blockader - while the side to move is not down material.

motifs.name: dangerous advanced passed pawn
motifs.description: The side to move owns a clearly more dangerous passed pawn than the opponent - advanced, unblockaded, with a clear or well controlled promotion path and pawn, neighbour-passer or heavy-piece support - while not being down material.

motifs.name: opponent moves keep walking into loss of material
motifs.description: A far larger share of the opponent possible moves would leave the moved piece capturable at a profit than of the side-to-move own moves, while the opponent has no capture that wins more material than the side to move can win, so the opponent is in a bind with hardly any safe option.

motifs.name: checking initiative against the enemy king
motifs.description: The side to move can deliver more safe checks (checking moves whose piece cannot be profitably captured) than the opponent could deliver if it were their turn, so it owns the forcing initiative.

motifs.name: enemy pawn over-extended into our camp
motifs.description: The opponent has a pawn that has pushed past the middle into the side-to-move half where no neighbouring enemy pawn can support it, and the side to move attacks that pawn while either blockading it or outnumbering its defenders, whereas the side to move has no such over-extended pawn itself and is not behind in material.

motifs.name: opponent burdened with two different kinds of weakness
motifs.description: The opponent camp holds targets of at least two different kinds - structurally weak pawns on half-open files, pieces under fire or about to be kicked by a pawn push, and a draughty or centralised king - and clearly more such targets in total than the side to move has at home, while the side to move is not down material.

motifs.name: favorable piece imbalance without a material lead
motifs.description: The side to move has no lead in raw material (standard 1/3/3/5/9 count is level within half a pawn), yet owns the structurally better army: the bishop pair in an open position, minor pieces traded against enemy pawns while pieces still dominate, two minors against a rook, knights in a locked pawn structure, or bishops in an open one. The armies must differ in composition - identical material on both sides never qualifies.

motifs.name: grip on the opponent weak colour complex
motifs.description: With material roughly level, the side to move keeps a bishop on a colour complex where the opponent has no bishop and few pawns, and grips the resulting unguarded squares of that colour in the opponent camp far more than the opponent grips the other complex.

motifs.name: true material edge hidden without a visible lead
motifs.description: The raw count shows no clear material lead for the side to move, yet it is really the one ahead: either it owns the stronger pieces in a material imbalance while standing slightly up on points, or an enemy piece has strayed into the half of the board belonging to the side to move where it has no safe square left and can be attacked more times than it is defended.

motifs.name: enemy queen harassed with tempo
motifs.description: The side to move can gain a tempo by safely attacking the opposing queen with a lesser piece, while its own queen cannot be harassed the same way and enjoys at least as many safe squares.

motifs.name: stronger double attack threat with nothing hanging
motifs.description: The side to move can make a safe move that sets up a bigger threat package (a fork, a hit on a more valuable or undefended enemy piece, or a threat combined with check) than the best threat the opponent could set up, while none of its own pieces are hanging or attacked by a cheaper unit.

motifs.name: enemy camp riddled with concrete pressure points
motifs.description: With material level or at most a pawn ahead, the side to move creates far more concrete problems in the opponent camp - hanging or pawn-harassed pieces, over-attacked units, pinned targets and pieces held only by a single overloaded or unstable guard - than the opponent creates against it.

motifs.name: opponent pieces cornered and hanging
motifs.description: Without holding more than a one-pawn material lead, the side to move troubles the opponent pieces far more than its own are troubled: more enemy knights, bishops, rooks and queens have at most one safe square available, and more of them stand attacked while undefended, hit by a cheaper unit, or attacked more times than defended.

motifs.name: tempo-gaining threat creation dominance
motifs.description: With material roughly level, the side to move has clearly more quiet moves that safely create a brand-new attack on an enemy unit (hitting it with a cheaper piece or hitting an undefended one) than the opponent can create in reply, so it keeps making threats with tempo.

motifs.name: more active king in a simplified position
motifs.description: With the queens traded and only a few pieces left, the side to move has the far more active king - more centralized, off its own back rank and closer to the pawns on the board - than the opponent, while not being behind in material.

motifs.name: line pressure with pins and x-rays
motifs.description: The side to move owns more line power against the opponent - absolute pins, x-ray alignments where a more valuable enemy unit stands behind a lesser one, sliders stacked in batteries and latent discovered-attack setups - than the opponent has in return.

metadata.score_definition: P(motif=True | winning) - P(motif=True | losing), measured on the discovery training dataset.
